title: 305. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Reading Piecewise Function Sign Intervals
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Sign Intervals of a Two-Piece Linear Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the negative intervals of a piecewise linear function from its algebraic rule.
questions.question: A piecewise function is defined by \(f(x)=x+1\) for \(x\le 0\), and \(f(x)=x-1\) for \(x>0\). On which intervals is \(f(x)<0\)?
questions.explanation: For \(x\le 0\), solve \(x+1<0\), which gives \(x<-1\). For \(x>0\), solve \(x-1<0\), which gives \(0<x<1\). Combining these gives \((-\infty,-1)\cup(0,1)\).
questions.hint: Solve the inequality separately on each piece and then combine the resulting intervals.

questions.concept: Sign Interval of a Piecewise Constant Function
questions.learningObjective: Identify the positive interval of a piecewise constant function described by its graph.
questions.question: A graph is defined by \(f(x)=-2\) for \(x<1\), and \(f(x)=3\) for \(x\ge 1\). On which interval is \(f(x)>0\)?
questions.explanation: On \(x<1\), the value is \(-2\), which is negative. On \(x\ge 1\), the value is \(3\), which is positive. Therefore, \(f(x)>0\) on \([1,\infty)\).
questions.hint: Check the sign of the constant value on each piece of the graph.

questions.concept: Positive Interval of a Two-Piece Linear Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the positive interval of a piecewise linear function by solving inequalities on each piece.
questions.question: A piecewise function is defined by \(f(x)=x+3\) for \(x<-1\), and \(f(x)=-x+1\) for \(x\ge -1\). On which interval is \(f(x)>0\)?
questions.explanation: For \(x<-1\), \(x+3>0\) gives \(x>-3\), so \((-3,-1)\). At \(x=-1\), the second piece gives \(2>0\). For \(x\ge -1\), \(-x+1>0\) gives \(x<1\), so \([-1,1)\). Combining these gives \((-3,1)\).
questions.hint: Solve \(x+3>0\) on the first piece and \(-x+1>0\) on the second piece, then join the intervals.

questions.concept: Negative Interval of a Quadratic-Linear Piecewise Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the negative interval of a piecewise function that changes from quadratic to linear.
questions.question: A piecewise function is defined by \(f(x)=x^2-4\) for \(x<0\), and \(f(x)=x-2\) for \(x\ge 0\). On which interval is \(f(x)<0\)?
questions.hint: Solve the inequality on each piece, then merge the intervals, noting the endpoint \(x=0\).

questions.concept: Positive Interval of a Two-Piece Linear Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the positive interval of a piecewise linear function from its rule.
questions.question: A piecewise function is defined by \(f(x)=2x-1\) for \(x<1\), and \(f(x)=3-x\) for \(x\ge 1\). On which interval is \(f(x)>0\)?
questions.explanation: For \(x<1\), \(2x-1>0\) gives \(x>1/2\), so \((1/2,1)\). At \(x=1\), the second piece gives \(2>0\). For \(x\ge 1\), \(3-x>0\) gives \(x<3\), so \([1,3)\). Combining these gives \((1/2,3)\).
questions.hint: Solve each linear inequality on its own piece and combine the positive intervals.

questions.concept: Negative Interval of a Quadratic-Linear Piecewise Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the negative interval of a piecewise function with a quadratic piece and a linear piece.
questions.question: A piecewise function is defined by \(f(x)=x^2-1\) for \(x\le 0\), and \(f(x)=x+2\) for \(x>0\). On which interval is \(f(x)<0\)?
questions.explanation: For \(x\le 0\), \(x^2-1<0\) gives \(-1<x<1\), so \((-1,0]\). For \(x>0\), \(x+2<0\) gives \(x<-2\), which is impossible on \(x>0\). Therefore, the negative interval is \((-1,0]\).
questions.hint: Solve the quadratic inequality on the first piece and check whether the second piece can ever be negative.

questions.concept: Positive Interval of a Two-Piece Linear Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the positive interval of a piecewise linear function with a break point.
questions.question: A piecewise function is defined by \(f(x)=-x+2\) for \(x<3\), and \(f(x)=x-4\) for \(x\ge 3\). On which intervals is \(f(x)>0\)?
questions.explanation: For \(x<3\), \(-x+2>0\) gives \(x<2\), so \((-\infty,2)\). For \(x\ge 3\), \(x-4>0\) gives \(x>4\), so \((4,\infty)\). Combining these gives \((-\infty,2)\cup(4,\infty)\).
questions.hint: Solve the inequality on each piece and note that the break point is \(x=3\).

questions.concept: Negative Interval of a Quadratic-Linear Piecewise Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the negative interval of a piecewise function by solving inequalities on both pieces.
questions.question: A piecewise function is defined by \(f(x)=x^2-4x+3\) for \(x<2\), and \(f(x)=2x-6\) for \(x\ge 2\). On which interval is \(f(x)<0\)?
questions.explanation: For \(x<2\), \(x^2-4x+3=(x-1)(x-3)<0\) gives \(1<x<3\), so \((1,2)\). At \(x=2\), the second piece gives \(-2<0\). For \(x\ge 2\), \(2x-6<0\) gives \(x<3\), so \([2,3)\). Combining these gives \((1,3)\).
questions.hint: Factor the quadratic on the first piece and solve the linear inequality on the second piece.

questions.concept: Positive Interval of an Absolute-Value and Quadratic Piecewise Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the positive interval of a piecewise function involving absolute value and a quadratic expression.
questions.question: A piecewise function is defined by \(f(x)=|x|-2\) for \(x<0\), and \(f(x)=x^2-4\) for \(x\ge 0\). On which intervals is \(f(x)>0\)?
questions.explanation: For \(x<0\), \(|x|-2=-x-2>0\) gives \(x<-2\), so \((-\infty,-2)\). For \(x\ge 0\), \(x^2-4>0\) gives \(x>2\), so \((2,\infty)\). Combining these gives \((-\infty,-2)\cup(2,\infty)\).
questions.hint: Replace \(|x|\) with \(-x\) on the first piece, then solve the resulting inequalities.

questions.concept: Positive Interval of a Three-Piece Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the positive interval of a three-piece function by analyzing each piece separately.
questions.question: A piecewise function is defined by \(f(x)=x+2\) for \(x<-1\), \(f(x)=x^2-1\) for \(-1\le x\le 2\), and \(f(x)=5-x\) for \(x>2\). On which intervals is \(f(x)>0\)?
questions.explanation: For \(x<-1\), \(x+2>0\) gives \(x>-2\), so \((-2,-1)\). For \(-1\le x\le 2\), \(x^2-1>0\) gives \(x<-1\) or \(x>1\), so within this piece the positive part is \((1,2]\). For \(x>2\), \(5-x>0\) gives \(x<5\), so \((2,5)\). Combining these gives \((-2,-1)\cup(1,5)\).
questions.hint: Analyze the sign on each of the three pieces, paying careful attention to the endpoints.
